title: Parliament approves grants to IMF trust funds for low-income countries and Sudan's debt relief
what_it_is: Two Motions moved by Minister of State Alvin Tan under section 6A(2)(d) of the Bretton Woods Agreements Act 1966, asking Parliament to fix the maximum amount of grants the Monetary Authority of Singapore may give to the IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust and to the PRG-HIPC Trust for Sudan's debt relief, debated together and voted on separately.
why_it_matters: The transcript states that the grant to the Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust will draw from Singapore's 2021 SDR allocation and reduce MAS' official foreign reserves by 21 million SDR, about US$28.6 million, while the grant to the PRG-HIPC Trust will be funded from Singapore's share of the IMF's existing resources and will not affect the size of MAS' official foreign reserves. Minister of State Alvin Tan said the contributions do not draw on past reserves and will not affect or reduce domestic expenditure for Singaporeans. The money supports the IMF's concessional lending to low-income countries and Sudan's debt relief under the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries Initiative.

key_points.point: Moves that the maximum grants MAS may give to the IMF's Poverty Reduction and Growth Trust is 21,000,000 Special Drawing Rights, about US$28,600,000
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: is 21,000,000 Special Drawing Rights, approximately US$28,600,000.

key_points.point: States he will move a second Motion for a separate grant of SDR 4.48 million, about US$6.1 million, to the PRG-HIPC Trust to support Sudan's debt relief
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: I will be moving a second Motion for a separate grant of SDR 4.48 million, approximately US$6.1 million to the IMF's Trust for the Special Poverty Reduction and Growth Operations for the Heavily Indebted Poor Countries (PRG-HIPC Trust), to support Sudan's debt relief.

key_points.point: Consents to a single debate on both Motions followed by two separate votes
key_points.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
key_points.quote: Yes, I give my consent to one debate and then two votes.

key_points.point: Says the Bretton Woods Agreements Act allows MAS to make grants through the IMF subject to four conditions
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: This is subject to four conditions.

key_points.point: Says Singapore received 3.73 billion SDR in the IMF's 2021 allocation although it did not need more resources
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Singapore received 3.73 billion in SDR, notwithstanding that we did not require an augmentation of our resources.

key_points.point: Says IMF annual lending commitments rose five-fold to 5.5 billion SDR per annum over 2020 to 2023, straining the PRGT's finances
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: The IMF's annual lending commitments increased five-fold compared to the pre-pandemic period to 5.5 billion SDR per annum during 2020 to 2023.

key_points.point: Says 45 member countries, including the United States, have pledged to contribute to the PRGT
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: with 45 member countries, including the United States (US), having also pledged to contribute to the PRGT

key_points.point: Says 122 members have pledged to contribute to Sudan's debt relief, including Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines and Thailand
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: with 122 members also having pledged to contribute, including our ASEAN-4 neighbours: Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines and Thailand.

key_points.point: Says the PRGT contribution reduces MAS' official foreign reserves by 21 million SDR, about US$28.6 million
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: resulting in a reduction of MAS' OFR by a relatively modest 21 million SDR, approximately US$28.6 million.

key_points.point: Says the PRG-HIPC contribution will be funded from Singapore's share of the IMF's existing resources and will not change the size of MAS' official foreign reserves
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: will not affect the size of MAS' OFR.

key_points.point: Says MAS issued a media release on 28 January 2026 and will publish key information about the grants in the Gazette after Parliament's resolution
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: MAS will publish in the Gazette key information about the grants.

key_points.point: Declares he works in a foreign bank and says he supports both Motions
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: I would like to declare that I work in a foreign bank.

key_points.point: Asks whether the proposed 21 million SDR limit includes the 14.5 million SDR approved by Parliament in a 2016 Motion
key_points.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
key_points.quote: Is this limit inclusive of the previous amount of 14.5 million SDR, approximately US$20 million, that this House passed in a 2016 Motion?

key_points.point: Declares he was for many years an employee at the Bretton Woods Institution and says he supports the Motion
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: I was for many years an employee at the Bretton Woods Institution, with which these two Motions are associated.

key_points.point: Asks why Sudan was selected for this round of debt relief rather than other HIPC countries
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: I would therefore like to understand the premise behind the selection of Sudan as the beneficiary of this round of relief.

key_points.point: Repeats his call for Singapore's official foreign development assistance to be institutionalised
key_points.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
key_points.quote: I return to my call first made more than three years ago that our official foreign development assistance be institutionalised.

key_points.point: Says the two Motions involve grants that are not repaid, capped and approved by Parliament
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
key_points.quote: these two Motions involve grants, which are not repaid.

key_points.point: Asks what options Singapore has to pause, reduce or recover overseas commitments if budgets tighten
key_points.speaker: Mr Ng Shi Xuan
key_points.quote: what options do we have to pause, reduce or recover overseas commitments, whether in the form of grants or loans

key_points.point: Says support for the PRGT is a form of early risk prevention
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
key_points.quote: support for the PRGT is not simply aid; it is a form of early risk prevention.

key_points.point: Says MAS has updated that 746 million SDR will be loaned to the IMF's Resilience and Sustainability Trust
key_points.speaker: Mr Shawn Loh
key_points.quote: MAS has updated that 746 million of SDR will be loaned to the IMF's RST.

key_points.point: Seeks clarification that the grants do not constitute a drawdown of Past Reserves
key_points.speaker: Mr Victor Lye
key_points.quote: these grants do not constitute a drawdown of Past Reserves

key_points.point: Says past contributions add to a common pool of PRGT resources and are not attributable to individual contributing members
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: our past contributions add to the common pool of resources for the PRGT and it is not attributable to individual contributing members.

key_points.point: Says the current 21 million SDR limit is a separate contribution and does not include the previous PRGT contribution
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: The proposed limit does not include the previous contribution to the PRGT.

key_points.point: Says the contributions do not draw on past reserves and will not affect or reduce domestic expenditure for Singaporeans
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: This set of contributions does not draw on our past Reserves, nor will it affect or reduce any domestic expenditure for Singaporeans.

key_points.point: Says the IMF has provided debt relief to 38 of the 39 eligible countries and Sudan is the last country eligible under the initiative
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: Of which, Sudan is the last country to be eligible under this initiative.

key_points.point: Says Singapore will join 22 other countries in supporting the IMF's RST and its initial fundraising target of 33 billion SDR
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: We will join 22 other countries in supporting the IMF to meet its initial fundraising target of 33 billion SDR.

key_points.point: Says Singapore's loan agreements with the IMF require the IMF to repay immediately if Singapore has a balance of payments need
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: the IMF is obliged to immediately repay the loan in the event Singapore has a balance of payments need.

key_points.point: Says the Prime Minister announced in April 2025 a new unit in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, now called the Development Strategy Unit
key_points.speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
key_points.quote: the Prime Minister announced the new unit in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then called the Development Partnership Unit and now the Development Strategy Unit

what_happens_next: Following Parliament's resolution, MAS will publish key information about the grants in the Gazette. Minister of State Alvin Tan also said the Government will put out additional public communications, such as social media posts, on Singapore's IMF contributions.
not_said: How much each other country is contributing to the two trusts, and how Singapore's contribution compares with theirs in absolute terms
Whether the earlier 14.5 million SDR contribution approved in 2016 has been drawn down
Whether the PRGT will reach a level that is financially self-sustaining, or whether further injections will be required
Whether grants of this nature are expected to remain occasional and case-specific or become regular
Whether Singapore's loan exposure under the Resilience and Sustainability Trust is expected to grow over time
Whether the earlier pledge of $1.25 billion to the PRGT has been fully disbursed
